utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar -- Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dan Saxon, Mark Harmon, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone participating in the proceedings. Mr. Perisic is represented today in the courtroom by Novak Lukic, Gregor Guy-Smith, and our assistant Boris Zorko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Just for the record, to note that the Chamber is still sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis in Judge Picard's absence. And good afternoon to you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, and good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. And, Mr. Simic, once again to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Mr. Lukic, sometime in the middle of yesterday's you had already used some five hours 20 minutes, and I am not quite sure how much you have used up to now. Are you still going to be long?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to tell you shortly, Your Honours. I know how much time we have envisaged for this witness. Actually, I would like to curtail the testimony of some other witnesses by virtue of this witness. Primarily by going through certain documents today we are considerably going to shorten another evidence and hopefully I will be finished by the end of the first session today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have given the documents to the OTP for them to review these documents. The documents that I'm going to look together with Mr. Simic today which will expedite the proceedings. We have given the binder in the B/C/S to the OTP but please can we have it back to the witness. We are going to follow the order of the documents, and this is the first one. Actually, we didn't manage to upload it because we have only received the translation today, and because of that, I have hard copies for all parties concerned. It will probably be uploaded in the course of today and then we shall have it in e-court. All the other documents already have their English translations and are in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we are going to continue with what we started yesterday. We are going to go through a number of documents relating to the work of the operations centre in certain relevant periods of times, and I will ask you some questions. The first document that I would like to show you, but for the time being we shall only see the B/C/S version on the screen, that's 65 ter 01254D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this the one which you have just given us the hard copy of?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's a report of the second administration of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army strictly confidential 189 of 9th July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am going to read only one portion which is going to be related to the next document. So if you look at this passage in the middle where units of the 1st Corps are being mentioned, General, can you tell us something about this which reads: "Units of the first K and parts of the 3rd, 2nd, and 7th KMV" et cetera. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units of the 1st Corps and elements of the 2nd, 3rd, and 7th Corps of the Muslim army continue preparation for the continuation of offensive activities aimed at lifting the blockade of the Muslim quarter of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please read the last sentence in this same passage. It starts with "units."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Units of the 28th Division from Srebrenica opened fire from the protected area with the support of the Dutch Battalion and they also used APCs of the Ukrainian battalion stationed in Zepa."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us just remind ourselves that these are intelligence reports based on which the operations centre produces its own report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would tender this document into evidence but pending the English translation it will only going to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document is admitted into evidence. Marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00216 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see that this document was dated 9th of July, 1995, and this is important for our next document which is 65 ter -- Prosecution, excuse me, Defence Exhibit 00490D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we are looking at is a daily operations report from your centre dated the 10th of July, 1995. Can you tell me which period is covered in this report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I said that daily operations reports covered 24 hours starting from 0600 hours on the previous day until 0600 hours of the current day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this would be for the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the daily operations report recorded on the 10th because it was completed during that night, a new day started, and that is when it was logged in the operations centre, but it refers to the period of daylight and the night of the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at paragraph 3, particularly its last part. This sentence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does it relate to the night of the 10th of July or the night of the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This refers to half of the night of the 10th from zero hundred hours until 2400 hours, which means from 6.00 in the morning on the 9th until 6.00 in the morning on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have read this sentence in the previous document, and now I am going to ask you if this sentence contained in the operations report, has it actually been copied or just slightly modified from that previous document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided a detailed explanation yesterday of the methodology of drafting reports, and when the shift meets at 2100 hours with duty officers from intelligence and operations administration, they extract from that report only those most relevant elements for the Chief of Staff and you can see this same sentence here saying that units from the 28th Division of Srebrenica opened fire from the protected area with the support of the Dutch Battalion and used the APCs of the Ukrainian Battalion stationed in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, once again, we would like to finish quickly so can you just listen to the question really and just focus in answering the question. Don't tell us what you told us yesterday, just say if the question was is this sentence mentioned here or just modified slightly, if it's yes, say yes, no, no. Then we can move on. Okay. Thank you, sir. I am sure you'd like to go home quickly too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more comment on this document, under item situation on the state border it is mentioned that the UN monitoring mission visited Zalvjne [phoen] border post of the 15th Battalion Bajina Basta and that there were no remarks. If the UN monitors had remarks, would those remarks be included in the report that was to be sent to the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more question relating to your testimony yesterday and the day before yesterday, you mentioned border battalions in Bajina Basta being part of the 1st Army. To whom was the Uzice Corps of the Yugoslav Army subordinated?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Drina valley south of the Sava river we had the 15th Border Battalion, 16th Battalion in Loznica and Bajina Basta. This is the line between areas of responsibility of the 1st and 2nd Army. The Battalion in Bajina Basta belonged to the Uzice Corps, and the Uzice Corps was part of the 2nd Army of Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Rumenko?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Rumenko Disovic was for a time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't object to the tendering of the document, just we are still waiting for an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't recorded precisely. I maybe put the interpreters in an awkward situation. If you can please repeat what you said about General Disovic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period General Disovic was commander of the Uzice Corps. I can't tell you the exact dates from to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00217.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that I would like the witness to see as well as the Chamber is 65 ter, Defence Exhibit 00682D. It's an intelligence report of 10th July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this report also submitted to your operations centre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions relating to this document, Your Honours. I just would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00218.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is also from the same group, 65 ter 00860D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope, General, that you have the documents in the right order, the way that I've been referring to them. This is an intelligence report compiled on the 11th of July, 1995. Again it's a document of the second administration. I would like to ask you for your comment on the last paragraph on the first page, General. Just a moment, please, let me have a look. The English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It must be on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have the second page in English. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please have your comments with regard to this information. Was it noteworthy in terms of this report of the operations centre, namely the Dutch aircraft to the south of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00219.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that I would like you to have a look at is 65 ter 00683D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is an intelligence report, also of the second administration dated the 12th of July, 1995, and I'd like to dwell on this document a bit longer. As far as I can see, if we look at these intelligence reports if they are sent to the operations centre, well, whose forces are you interested in describing, whose activities in the reports of the operations centre? Are you interested in the activities of the BH Army, the Muslim army, or the Army of Republika Srpska? What is primarily the function of what is contained in the reports of the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intelligence report is a report of the operations administration, and it follows the other side, the adversary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first two paragraphs we see that there's a detailed description of the units of the BH Army and in the third sentence it says: "During the morning of the 12th of July, 1995, units of the Drina Corps of the VRS entered Potocari." Isn't that right? And then there is further information about the Croatian army. This report of the 12th of July of the second administration, when was it processed in your daily operations report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have been processed in the daily operations report of the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, could we please get a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00220.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the next document that I would like to show is document that is marked 65 ter 00491D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is now a report of the first administration, the operations centre. The date is the 13th of July, 1995. General, I'm glad that you have both documents in front of you so that you can compare them. In the first part there is a reference to the activities of the armed forces of neighbouring countries. Is there anything that was not included and where the report of the operations centre does not coincide with what the intelligence report says?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, the content is there, although it may have been worded differently in the daily operations report because that is a result of the sublimation of the material involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The sentence we read out a few moments ago from the intelligence report and the third paragraph, namely: "During the morning of the 12th of July, 1995 the units of the Drina Corps entered the village of Potocari." I do not see that in the daily operations report, right? All the rest is identical.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry if this was a leading question, but I thought that the content of the document cannot really be challenged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, that means that the document is processed in terms of what is important for the Chief of General Staff to know and what is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could I please have your comments, we don't need to read it out loud, but could you give us your comments on the first two paragraphs of the second section, the situation at the state border. Could we just hear your comments because the activities of the monitoring mission are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The monitoring mission observed the border and the situation at the border and also the observance of the border regime. We see here that they inspected a bridge that had been taken out and that was not being used.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether this was an every-day activity?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that it was an every-day activity, but it was frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00221.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreters request that when the witness is speaking, all other microphones be switched off, so if you would please remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Could we now please have a look at the next document, and that is 65 ter 00690D. It's a Defence document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report of the second administration dated the 13th of July, 1995. And I would like you to have a look at the first paragraph, General. Because of the relevance of the documents that are yet to come, I'm going to read it out loud. The first paragraph reads as follows: "Units of the Army of Republika Srpska have routed the 28th PD" - I assume it's infantry division - "of the Muslim army from Srebrenica. In this area, the M/V forces," probably the Muslim army forces, "are no longer putting up an organised defence. The routed elements of the 28th infantry division (5.000 to 6.000 men) made during the night of the 12th and 13th of July an unsuccessful element to break through in the direction of Kladanj and Tuzla. The largest group was surrounded in the sector of Kamenica and the village of Siljkovici and was given an ultimatum to surrender. In the fighting so far, about 500 members of the M/V, Muslim army, have been taken prisoner. From the Srebrenica area, so far about 50 per cent of the Muslim residents have been evacuated. The evacuation of the remaining residents is impeded by shortage of vehicles." General, for you at the operations centre, was the movement of the 28th Division of the Muslim army an important military movement at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that Zepa is near the border, sorry not Zepa, Srebrenica, I do apologise. It is near the border with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and these forces that I described here during their withdrawal and during their attempted break-through, part of them could have headed across the border towards the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Therefore, it was important to take measures of heightened security along the state border so that such armed persons would not cross the border, or rather, even if they were to cross the border, that we act in accordance with the border service rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is the border service rule, if such persons cross the border of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained yesterday that in the border belt that is the capture and surrender of these persons, the disarming, and their hand over to the organs of the Ministry of the Interior. At that point our authority over those persons ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could I please tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00222.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that was the report of the 13th of July. Could we now look at Defence document 65 ter 00492D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are going to have the report of the operations centre of the first administration from the next day, the 14th of July, 1995. I don't want to read it, but I'm just going to ask you whether the third paragraph in your daily operations report which corresponds to the third paragraph of the English version, does it faithfully reflect what we read out a few moments ago from the intelligence report on this particular topic, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the importance of the information involved, this was fully reflected in the daily operations report for the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am going to ask you for another brief comment. Actually, we don't really need to deal with it now. I was thinking of a comment regarding the state border, but it's actually similar to what we've already heard. Or actually, let it not appear that I'm trying to skip something. Your comment regarding the monitoring mission, it says here what they were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is section number 2 of this document. Situation on the state border. The first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't want to read it, I'd just like to hear the witness's comment.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can be seen here is that the members of the monitoring mission were allowed to enter the border belt and to monitor the regime along the border. And what is written here is what they actually did, what they observed. Also, there were no violations of the border regime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00223.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have Defence document 00691D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report now dated the 14th of July, 1995. I would like to draw your attention, Mr. Simic, to a particular paragraph that is towards the end, Your Honours. The last two paragraphs in the English version, I don't really need to have to read out into the transcript. But could you please give us your comment. It has do with two particular pieces of information received by the intelligence administration.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it also says that the crushed parts of the 28th Division are continuing towards Kladanj and Tuzla and they are trying to get out of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The term used is they are trying to avoid being destroyed by the VRS. Is that customary usage, this particular word in military terminology?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. And one more thing should be added, that is what happens if they are asked to surrender and they put up resistance rather than surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also have some information on Zepa here. That was an ultimatum that was not honoured, and then the offensive against Zepa started. Was this an information that was important for being entered into your operations report?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not hear the answer at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreter said they could not hear the answer at all, so we don't have it interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question, General. Was this information customarily used in military terminology, destroying enemy units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the admission of the document, but Mr. Lukic actually asked for an answer to a question that had been answered. The question that was not answered is at line -- begins at line 17 of page 15 of the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may have a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just to be sure what you are talking about, Mr. Saxon, line 17 is the middle of an answer which starts at line 16 on my screen yes, yes, absolutely, and one more thing should be added, that is, what happens if they are asked to surrender and they put up resistance rather than surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I beg the Court's pardon, Your Honour, the question is on page 15, lines 21 to 22: "Was this an information that was important for being entered into your operations report?" Then the interpreter says, "We could not hear the answer at all."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't believe that question --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question referred to Zepa, and I asked about this piece of information relating to Zepa and, please, General, repeat your answer. What is written here in relation to an offensive on Zepa, was that a piece of information deemed important enough to be entered into the report of the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Have we given it a number? May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00224.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter Defence document 00493D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's an intelligence report of the first administration operations centre of the 15th of July. General, please focus on the middle part where it says, The broken up parts, et cetera. I'm not going to read it. But what is written here by the operations centre completely corresponds to what we read a minute ago in the report from the second administration?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00225.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have on our screens 00692D, Defence document. That's a report produced by the second administration on the 15th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are probably going to have to recall Exhibit D230.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, the document that is Exhibit D230 now, 495 was its 65 ter number. It's on the first page in B/C/S, and I believe that is the case in English too.

utterances.text: I guess --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Situation at the state border --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go back to the previous document, yes. D230, and could we please have the English version on the screen as well. And do you see the situation at the state border? [English] First paragraph, last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My concern is in the text of the transcript, maybe it was not interpreted properly, but at page 23, line 1, it says: "We can see two persons, armed persons, were captured at the border," and that's what I read in the first paragraph is that there is some -- a single person without weapons who was captured. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess it's in the next page, Mr. Lukic. I saw something like -- somebody and the lieutenant, and the lieutenant had a gun on him on the document. Can we go to the next page, please. Mr. Lukic is not listening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the important thing is that the Prosecution wants to see that passage on the exhibit. They are asking to be directed to the paragraph that relates to that story. I thought it was on this page, but it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I just have a look, please, at the transcript, Your Honours, so that I can find the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Page 23, line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, lest there be any misunderstanding, could you please give us your comment in view of what the transcript says. utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the area of Banja Koviljaca a Muslim soldier was caught Selimovic, Sead without any weapons. Borne --"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't have to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "-- wearing civilian clothes. He denies that he was a member of the armed forces, he was handed over to the organs of the Ministry of the Interior of Loznica."

utterances.text: Mr. Simic, please listen to your lawyer when he talks to you. He says you don't have to read that. He wants you to comment. Now you have read it to us, can you comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The second piece of information in the next paragraph, what location, what border crossing does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the 10th Border Battalion, Ulcinj, if that's the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether we've clarified the matter now in view of the sentence that was originally recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I think it has been clarified because the sentence at page 23, line 1, isn't reflected in the exhibit. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] But at line 23 -- at page 23 he is talking of two persons but here it's one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON

utterances.text: I'd just like a brief comment from you, General. It has to do with what we've been following all along. utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've lost continuity, Mr. Lukic, in terms of following the numbers. 496D is the next document that I have.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at one more document before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please skip two documents, General. Look at the daily operations centre report of 22nd of July, 1995. And the 65 ter number is 660D. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it please be shown to the Court as well. That is the situation on the state border. So it's probably page 2 in the English version. And in the Serbian version as well.

utterances.text: You see that the members of the mission have no objections, but right in the middle it says: "On the 21st of July, information was received from Ljubovija, et cetera, and this gives specific information about a convoy." utterances.text: This information was received from the report of the army commander.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: That's not an answer to the question, Mr. Simic. The question is in whose area of responsibility?

utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not received directly from the border people, but the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the end of your sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The report was not received from the border people but from the report of the commander of the 1st Army in whose area of responsibility that border unit is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would suggest that we take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have it admitted into evidence, please.
